findings.title: Cache miss is re-checked only by the fast path, so concurrent callers all rebuild the manifest
findings.body: The read lock is released at line 43 and the write lock is taken at line 48 without re-checking `entryPointAssetsCache`. When the cache is empty or in dev mode, every goroutine that misses the cache at the same moment proceeds to call readWebAssetsFromFile (or the CDN path) and rebuilds the manifest, one after another. The usual fix is to re-read the cache after acquiring the write lock and return early if it is already populated. This only matters at startup or in dev mode, so the impact is limited to redundant file reads and parsing.

findings.title: Write lock is held across file and network I/O, blocking all readers
findings.body: The exclusive lock taken at line 48 is held for the whole rebuild, including the HTTP request in readWebAssetsFromCDN and the file read. Every concurrent GetWebAssets call, including ones that would otherwise hit the cached fast path, blocks on RLock until the rebuild finishes. A slow or hung CDN request, bounded only by the context, can stall all page renders. Consider doing the load outside the lock and only publishing the result under the lock.

findings.title: No regression test for the data race fix
findings.body: The PR fixes an unsynchronized read of the package-level `entryPointAssetsCache`, but adds no test that exercises GetWebAssets from multiple goroutines. A test run under `go test -race` that calls GetWebAssets concurrently (with the cache populated and in dev mode) would catch a regression of this fix. Without one, the lock discipline could be broken again silently.
